rationale: The buyer is a specific, nameable person — a pre-Series A SaaS founder in an active fundraising process — who faces real financial stakes (losing a deal) and has demonstrated willingness to pay for analogous services (law firm DD packages, Notion template marketplaces). However, pain_frequency is low (founders go through DD once or twice in a lifetime), which sharply limits LTV and repeat revenue, and with a total of 6.0 the idea falls just below the 6.5 build threshold. The operational_autonomy gate is narrowly met (Claude can generate DD checklists and draft document packs without per-customer human work), but the single-event nature of the pain and the absence of any responsiveness signal mean validation — not building — is the right next step.
solution_plan: The micro-service is an AI-powered investor due-diligence preparation kit: the founder fills in a 10-question intake form (stage, ARR, incorporation type, investor type) and receives a tailored DD checklist, a prioritised document-gap analysis, and draft narrative answers to the 15 most common investor questions — all generated by Claude and delivered as a PDF/Notion export within minutes. BUILD: the factory creates a Claude prompt chain, a Tally or Typeform intake form, a simple landing page (Carrd or similar), and a Stripe payment link at ~$97-$197 one-time; no coding by the operator. SELL: reach founders via Y Combinator's forum, Indie Hackers, and LinkedIn searches for 'raising seed / Series A' posts; also target accelerator alumni communities (Techstars, MassChallenge); outreach batches go out only after operator approval. MAINTAIN: Stripe handles billing, Claude handles document generation triggered by form submission, and delivery is automated via email; the only recurring operator touch is approving outreach batches and reviewing any refund requests. CAVEAT: because this is a one-time-purchase product (low repeat rate), validate willingness to pay at the $97-$197 price point with at least 5 paying customers before investing further — if conversion is weak at that price the unit economics do not work for a solo operator.
notes: All four build_gates are narrowly met (operational_autonomy=7, buildability_with_ai=8, buyer_clarity=7, willingness_to_pay=6), so the stage is not gate-capped — it is held at validate purely because the weighted_total of 6.0 is below the 6.5 build threshold. The key risk is low pain_frequency (one-time event per founder lifecycle), which suppresses LTV and makes CAC recovery fragile. Validate with a pre-sell or waitlist before building.
